scorecard.note: Make the arc feel more like a story—connect the data points with a clear narrative of widening inequality rather than a simple list of statistics.

storyboard.ears: Your paycheck decides how long you get to live, and the gap is growing.
Richest American men outlive the poorest men by 14.6 years. That is more than a decade of life, lost to a paycheck.
storyboard.eyes: substance: lit birthday candles; cause: Data places one more lit candle on the rich man's cake for every extra birthday he lives
storyboard.evidence: JAMA (Journal of the American Medical Association) | US life expectancy gap, richest vs poorest 1% by income | https://www.equality-of-opportunity.org/ | 2026-11-13

storyboard.ears: Sixty years of progress added only about 9 years to American lives. The richest-poorest gap beats all of it.
storyboard.evidence: CDC National Center for Health Statistics | US average life expectancy at birth, 1960-2023 | https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/fastats/life-expectancy.htm | 2026-11-13

storyboard.ears: Since 2001, the richest fifth of Americans gained 2.3 years of life. The poorest fifth got almost nothing.
storyboard.evidence: JAMA (Journal of the American Medical Association) | Life expectancy gained since 2001, by income group | https://www.equality-of-opportunity.org/ | 2026-11-13

storyboard.ears: Money doesn't just buy comfort. It buys years, and that gap keeps growing.
